title: Anthropic's Revenue Hits $65 Billion Run Rate as IPO Could Reach $2 Trillion Valuation
excerpt: The AI company's annualized revenue surged from $9 billion at the end of 2025, but investors are pressing executives on AI backlash, regulatory risks, and pricing pressure ahead of a potential October listing.
body:
• Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reached $65 billion at the end of July, up from $9 billion at the end of 2025, with some investors expecting it to hit $100 billion this year
  • The company could seek a valuation of $2 trillion or more in an October IPO, which would make it the largest public offering on record
  • Anthropic is addressing investor concerns about AI backlash, Trump administration tensions, and growing competition from cheaper Chinese AI models
  • The company has raised nearly $100 billion in private capital in 2026 and reached a $965 billion valuation in May

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude assistant, is barreling toward what could become the largest initial public offering in history, with some investors projecting a valuation of $2 trillion or more for an October debut. But the company faces a growing list of challenges that are forcing it to address investor skepticism head-on.

The company's annualized revenue run rate reached $65 billion at the end of July, Bloomberg reported, representing a remarkable surge from $9 billion at the end of 2025. Some investors expect that figure to reach $100 billion before year-end, according to the Financial Times.

A Race for Capital

Anthropic filed paperwork with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, entering a quiet period. The company has raised just under $100 billion from venture capital firms, sovereign wealth funds, and institutional investors in 2026 alone, reaching a $965 billion valuation in May when it surpassed OpenAI for the first time.

"If Anthropic is growing 800% a year, you'd think at the incredibly low end they would trade at 30 times revenue. That would make them a $3 trillion company."

— Anthropic investor, speaking to the Financial Times

The listing would put Anthropic in direct competition with SpaceX, which went public at a $1.77 trillion valuation in June, for a finite pool of investor capital. OpenAI has pushed its own IPO to next year, with its annualized revenue recently crossing $40 billion — roughly doubling from end-2025 but still well behind Anthropic's pace.

Investors Press on Risks

In pre-IPO meetings, investors have pressed Anthropic executives on a range of concerns, according to the Wall Street Journal. The company faces a growing backlash in Silicon Valley, where chief executives have grown nervous about its power over the AI ecosystem. Data-center construction has drawn public opposition in communities across the United States.

Regulatory headwinds have already had a tangible impact. The Commerce Department's export controls forced Anthropic to briefly remove its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models in June, an episode that two investors said slowed revenue growth and raised concerns among enterprise customers.

The company also remains in litigation with the Defense Department, which labeled it a supply-chain risk earlier this year, and has faced broader pressure from the Trump administration.

Pricing Pressure Emerges

Perhaps most critically for the long-term investment case, businesses are beginning to watch their AI spending more carefully. Ramp data showed that companies are "hitting their limit on AI spend" and shifting some workloads to cheaper systems.

Anthropic's top model costs more than two and a half times as much as OpenAI's flagship, according to Artificial Analysis. Chinese open-weight models are considerably cheaper still. As companies move from pilot programs to large-scale deployments, the price gap is becoming a factor in procurement decisions.

The IPO's outcome will set the tone for how public markets value frontier AI companies. Trillions of dollars in AI infrastructure spending rest on the assumption that demand for the technology will continue to accelerate — and Anthropic's listing will be the first real test of whether public investors share that conviction.
